cards.name: price-co-residency-and-per-bucket-overhead-before-buying-gri-composable-gfx950-decode
cards.description: Narrow-N bf16 decode GEMM behind a dispatch overlay: pipeline the K loop deeper at modest split-K instead of raising split-K for CU fill; 1.081x lane
cards.key: bf16 A16W16 decode GEMM cluster served through a Python dispatch overlay over a DSL hgemm family, graded per shape bucket against a frozen live-serving baseline · gfx950/MI355X
cards.effect: 1.081x isolated (director-verified vs the frozen baseline); per case the retuned narrow-N M=64 decode bucket gained ~1.087x in clean device time yet only ~1.003x of its scored latency (~+0.3% weighted at ~22% weight), the two M=1024 prefill cases run ~1.21-1.23x, and the two M=64 decode cases stay ~0.99x inherited
cards.roofline: grid-fill-bound by appearance only: the heaviest decode case is already fully co-resident (LDS per workgroup allows 2 WG/CU, so all CTAs fit in one wave) and runs at ~29% of achievable HBM; ~69% and ~47% of the two laggard buckets' scored latency is geometry-invariant per-call cost, capping all kernel-side work at a ~1.95x Amdahl ceiling
cards.title: Price co-residency and per-bucket overhead before buying grid fill on a narrow-N decode GEMM
cards.lever: when a decode bucket looks starved (CTA count far below CU count), try a shorter, deeper-pipelined K loop first — halve the k tile so the block-K loop runs more iterations, raise the pipeline stage count, keep split-K small — rather than raising split-K or coarsening tiles to manufacture CTAs.
cards.apply: a per-shape geometry constant selected inside the overlay at one exact M bucket and dtype, with fallthrough to the caller's own geometry for every other key; gate it with a build-time mirror of the launcher's split-K capacity check so an over-tiled geometry is refused where it is chosen.
cards.stack:
total 1.081x isolated (director-verified vs the frozen baseline) = an inherited per-shape routing plus two rounds that added no score
- stack:   1. per-shape backend routing inherited in the seed — carries the whole positive metric (both prefill cases and the M=1 decode case); not isolated by this lane
- stack:   2. dispatch-layer route census + predicate narrowed to the one scored M bucket — score-neutral by design (round 1, verified); it removed a 3-54% latent regression on unscored captured shapes
- stack:   3. the K-loop retune above — ~1.09x clean device time on its bucket, ~+0.3% weighted attributable (round 2, verified), left unadopted
- stack:   note: attribution is incremental in landing order; (3)'s scored share sits inside this box's own session drift, so it is reported as directional (lower in 3 of 3 interleaved pairs), not as an isolated split.
cards.verify: before funding the round, measure the bucket's amplification: time a same-route case carrying a fraction of the arithmetic (M=1 against M=64 here); if it costs about the same, that fraction of the denominator is geometry-invariant and a clean-kernel ratio arrives at the score divided by it — set the target from the derated figure, and recompute every headline from per-case medians over ALL graded buckets.
cards.pitfall:
raising split-K to fill CUs got monotonically slower on two independent ladders -> this family's split-K reduce is a global-semaphore spin-wait plus signal ring, so the barrier dominates a short kernel -> keep split-K small and buy the overlap from stage depth instead.
- pitfall: every re-tile trading CTA count for CTA size lost monotonically -> there was no tail wave to fill: LDS per workgroup allowed 2 WG/CU, so all CTAs were already co-resident -> count resident CTA slots from LDS-per-workgroup before calling a bucket underfilled.
- pitfall: widened k tiles passed the source's own tiling validator and then failed oracle parity (relative error 0.35-1.29 vs the torch reference) -> the validator only checks the k tile modulo 32, not that it divides the real K -> take as the legal set only the k tiles that clear a parity probe at the graded K.
- pitfall: an over-tiled split-K geometry raised on a live hot-path call rather than at build -> the capacity check runs inside the launcher -> mirror it as a build-time guard where the geometry is picked.
- pitfall: sequential single-shot A/B moved an unchanged binary by up to 12%, and the same config drifted ~2% within one session on this shared box -> clock/thermal drift -> randomised interleaved duels with medians across rounds, and a printed harness headline that silently graded 7 of 8 buckets is not comparable across runs.
cards.caution: also verify parity across repeated launches of the SAME config on any skinny-M path that raises split-K here: one config returned bit-correct output once and large errors on five of six launches, consistent with a shared split-K semaphore/signal pair the epilogue leaves un-rezeroed.
cards.source: run e2e-gpt-oss-120b bf16 A16W16 decode GEMM cluster lane, 2 rounds, director-validated 2026-09-09
